title: Long A Teams
kidRule: When two letters team up to say long A, AI usually goes in the middle of a word and AY goes at the end. Crayon is a sneaky one: its AY sits at the end of the first beat, CRAY-on!
hint: Listen for the long A and clap the beats. Is the sound tucked in the middle of a beat or right at the end of one? That tells you which team to pick.
reminder: Long A is spelled A-I in the middle and A-Y at the end of a word or beat.

check.question: Why does YESTERDAY end with AY and not AI?
check.correctAnswer: Long A at the end of a word is usually spelled AY!
distractors: Because AI is only used in long words
Because Y always comes after the letter A

words.def: To say that you are unhappy about something.
words.sent: My brother likes to complain when it is time for bed.
words.story: Grown-up cats hardly ever meow at other cats. They save their meows for people, often to complain that dinner is late!
words.card: Do not *complain* that your toast is *plain*, the jam is on vacation!

words.sent: We flew our kite at the park yesterday.
words.story: Because of time zones, when it is Monday morning in New Zealand it is still yesterday, Sunday, in Hawaii!
words.card: *Yes*, *yesterday* I taught a T. rex to tie my shoes!

words.def: A stick of colored wax for drawing.
words.sent: I used a red crayon to color the apple.
words.story: This word comes from French, where 'craie' means chalk!
words.card: A *ray* of sunshine melted my *crayon* into a rainbow puddle!

words.def: A make-believe sea creature that is half woman and half fish.
words.sent: The mermaid in the story had a shiny green tail.
words.story: Long ago, sailors who saw manatees from far away sometimes thought they were mermaids!
words.card: The *mermaid* hired a lobster *maid* to tidy her coral bedroom!

words.def: To show something so people can look at it.
words.sent: The museum will display our class paintings.
words.story: A peacock spreads out his giant tail feathers to display them when he wants to impress a peahen!
words.card: The peacock stopped his *play* to *display* his fancy feathers!

words.def: The part that is left over, like the extra bit after you divide.
words.sent: Ten divided by three is three with a remainder of one.
words.story: A year is about 365 days with a remainder of almost 6 hours. Those hours add up to one extra day every four years, and that is a leap year!
words.card: My *main* job is to eat the *remainder* of the cookies!

words.sent: The puppy was afraid of the loud thunder.
words.story: When you feel afraid, your heart beats faster to get your body ready to run or jump out of the way!
words.card: The mouse was *afraid*, so the cat brought first *aid* and a cupcake!

words.def: To tell about something so that others can understand it.
words.sent: Can you explain how the game works?
words.story: This word comes from a Latin word that means 'to make flat and smooth'. When you explain something, you smooth out the tricky bumps!
words.card: Please *explain* why there is a penguin in my *plain* pasta!

words.def: To keep people happy and interested by doing something fun for them.
words.sent: A juggler came to entertain the children at the fair.
words.story: Hundreds of years ago, jesters were hired to entertain kings and queens with jokes, songs, and juggling!
words.card: *Enter* the tent and I will *entertain* you with my dancing socks!

words.def: A thick, creamy white spread made from eggs and oil.
words.sent: He spread mayonnaise on both slices of bread.
words.story: Mayonnaise is made by whisking oil into egg yolks a little at a time until the two blend into a thick cream!
words.card: *May* I please have *mayonnaise* on my birthday cake? No? Okay!
